items.item: `Sources/Parsers/Parsers.Integer.swift`: `allowLeadingZeros: false` skips leading zeros instead of rejecting
items.reason: Decimal with allowLeadingZeros: false now throws the new Parsers.Integer.Error.leadingZero when a 0 is followed by another digit; a lone 0 still parses. Tests added.

Climbing has no failure of its own (Failure == Atom.Failure), so after applying a .none operator it stops before another operator of the same precedence and leaves it unconsumed (1<2<3 parses 1<2, input left at '<3'), the same way it stops on an unparseable right operand. Tests for this and for postfix operators added.
Last line drops its trailing LF (or CRLF); pinned test updated, CRLF test added.

api_changes: Parsers.Integer.Error gains public case leadingZero (non-frozen public enum)
dependents: none found: no package outside swift-parsers switches on Parsers.Integer.Error or uses allowLeadingZeros or Diagnostic.Source.line
notes: Not built; swiftc -parse and swift format run on changed files.
